cento-e-oitenta-e-nove-mil-paginas.t: One hundred and eighty-nine thousand pages
cento-e-oitenta-e-nove-mil-paginas.s: Nobody will read it all. What can be known before opening the first one.

inq-5026-01-doze-bilhoes-e-duas-associac.s: A Central Bank letter in March 2025, a reply naming civil-servant associations in Bahia as the origin of R$ 6.7 billion in loans, and a shelf company renamed two days before signing the contract. Where Operation Compliance Zero began.

inq-5026-02-o-lado-do-brb.s: A state-owned bank that, according to the record, bought loan portfolios worth 30% of its own assets, breached its Basel ratio, accepted repayment in instalments against the contract and, according to the police, really just wanted to lend. What the record says about the buyer.

inq-5026-03-dezoito-de-novembro.s: Five pre-trial detentions, two temporary ones, a bank president removed, an order for the Central Bank to intervene in BRB and, the same day, the liquidation of Master. Then a flight to Dubai that became an argument, a court that said no and, ten days later, said yes.

inq-5026-04-o-parlamentar-na-gaveta.s: A document seized at a suspect's home, a complaint to the Supreme Court, a duty judge who suspended everything on a December night, a prosecutor who called it turmoil, and the inquiry that moved up anyway.

inq-5026-05-o-inquerito-vira-balcao.s: Under the new reporting justice, from February 2026, Inquiry 5.026 starts receiving everything: invitations from the Senate, safe-conducts for the congressional inquiry committee, a former Central Bank governor who did not want to go, congressmen asking to include other congressmen, and the Central Bank flagging a second conglomerate. What the justice did with each.

pet-15198-01-de-sao-paulo-a-brasilia.s: An inquiry born of an anonymous PDF, a request to freeze R$ 5.7 billion, a judge who asks for explanations and a justice who pulls everything up to the Supreme Court. How the second phase of the operation changed address.

pet-15198-02-a-maquina-de-fundos.s: A clinic with R$ 54 thousand in revenue that issued R$ 361 million in notes. A bank that was the sole quotaholder of the funds buying the paper. What the police and the prosecutors say they found, in their own words.

pet-15198-03-a-madrugada-de-14-de-janeir.s: A flight to Dubai at 00:50, another to Curitiba at 07:30, a justice furious with the Federal Police and a temporary detention that lasted until seven in the morning. The second phase, hour by hour.

pet-15198-04-o-novo-relator-e-os-cem-apa.t: The new reporting justice and the hundred devices
pet-15198-04-o-novo-relator-e-os-cem-apa.s: In February the petition changes hands. The new justice writes about compartmentalisation quoting himself in Spanish, sends the forensic work back to the Federal Police, grants safe-conducts for the congressional inquiry and, in June, splits the investigation out of the drawer.

pet-15198-05-os-carros.s: An Aston Martin, a Bentley, two financed Porsches, thirteen registered guns and R$ 184,750 in cash. What the suspects asked to get back, what the State answered, and why the answer is always the same.

pet-15556-01-setenta-e-duas-horas.s: How a 164-page request from the Federal Police became, in five days, a 48-page ruling. What it is, what it is not, and why the prosecutors asked for more time and did not get it.

pet-15556-02-a-turma.s: A million a month, split six ways. What the ruling says about the surveillance and intimidation cell, in the words of the messages the police transcribed.

pet-15556-03-o-supervisor-que-revisava-o.s: Two heads of the Central Bank department that supervised Master, a group chat, a consultancy for 'bringing young people into the financial market' and the sentence 'today we have to pay Belline's first one'.

pet-15556-04-o-que-o-ministro-decidiu-e-.t: What the justice decided, and how
pet-15556-04-o-que-o-ministro-decidiu-e-.s: The law requires three things to detain someone before trial. The ruling says it found all three, explains why, and then spends seven pages teaching how to make an arrest properly.

pet-15556-05-depois-do-decreto.s: From 4 March to 24 July 2026, in the same docket: a transfer to a federal penitentiary, a death, four safe-conducts, a father arguing over two billion and the securities regulator wanting to hear the detainee.

rcl-88121-01-a-pasta.s: In a search at a banker's home, the Federal Police collected a folder bearing a congressman's name. In the seizure report, the name vanished. The defence took that detail to the Supreme Court and, with it, the whole case. The reporting justice's first order was about the value of the claim.

rcl-88121-02-nove-de-dezembro.s: The injunction that suspended the Brasília investigation for all suspects, not only as regards the congressman; the order that the Central Bank comply with no one else's decision; and the week in which the INSS congressional inquiry, a social network and a bank searched by mistake all knocked on the same door.

rcl-88121-03-vinte-e-dois-de-dezembro.s: A São Paulo judge who refused to send Operation Quasar to the Supreme Court, a prosecutors' opinion that agreed with caution but defended the trial court, and the final decision: the Supreme Court keeps the case because, among everyone named, there is evidence against a single person with privileged venue.

rcl-88121-04-trinta-e-nove-bilhoes.s: The Central Bank answered the Supreme Court's order with a seven-page report and 58 attachments. In it is the arithmetic the press never closed: how much BRB bought from Master, how much it returned, what it received in exchange, and what the supervisor itself ordered provisioned.

rcl-88121-05-o-arquivo-que-nao-fecha.t: The file that will not close
rcl-88121-05-o-arquivo-que-nao-fecha.s: The complaint became final in February 2026 and was archived. After that it received a Central Bank leak to the federal audit court, a letter from the president of the INSS congressional inquiry, a new reporting justice, and a string of billion-real requests from BRB, from the Federal District and from a lawyer in another operation.

inq-5035-01-projeto-dv.s: A city councillor from Rio Grande do Sul posted a video saying he had been offered money to attack the Central Bank. Twelve days later the Federal Police had a survey of 22 profiles, an opening order and a code name taken from a non-disclosure agreement. How the smallest inquiry in the archive was born.

inq-5035-02-duas-testemunhas.s: A councillor who signed the non-disclosure agreement to find out what it was about, and a journalist who hung up before finding out. The two statements of 12 February 2026, the notarial records, the penalty of eight hundred thousand reais that the contract spells out as two hundred, and what nobody managed to prove.

inq-5035-03-quem-pediu-para-entrar.t: Who asked to be let in
inq-5035-03-quem-pediu-para-entrar.s: The agency owner who asked for access to the inquiry before the inquiry existed, the journalist served notice at an old e-mail address, a 45-day medical certificate, a senator who says he was the target of a search, and a queue of lawyers in a case to which, since May, the police have added nothing.

pet-15478-01-o-que-os-celulares-disseram.t: What the police read on the phones
pet-15478-01-o-que-os-celulares-disseram.s: In February 2026 the Federal Police took to the Supreme Court the first excerpts from the phones seized in November. A director with a chill down his spine, a bank owner asking to correct a statement, a treasurer who finds it hard to register a lien, and a BRB director's notebook. The representation that opened Petition 15.478.

pet-15478-02-treze-nomes.s: Nine people, four companies, two years of accounts and tax returns. The list the police asked for, the crime attributed to each, the prosecutors' opinion that agreed in three weeks and the ruling that took three more months to say yes.

pet-15478-03-o-que-os-bancos-devolveram.s: Seventy-eight institutions notified by the Central Bank, files with thousands of rows transmitted through a system called Simba, a company the tax authority says has been closed since 2018, and the realisation that the data that matter are not in the record, and never will be.

pet-15504-01-a-denuncia-anonima.s: On the afternoon of 7 January 2026 someone told the Central Bank's president, without giving a name, that two heads of bank supervision had taken money from Master's owner. By 5:30 pm the director of supervision was already hearing the first of them. Within two days the case was with the Federal Police; within seven weeks, at the Supreme Court.

pet-15504-02-prioridade-absoluta.s: One hundred and thirty-one pages about an iPhone. What the Federal Police say they found in the banker's conversations with the two supervisors: drafts reviewed by their own addressee, tips for a meeting with the Central Bank's president, a monitoring filter that 'went off', a three-person group called Master and a meeting on the eve of the liquidation.

pet-15504-03-carta-convite.s: A youth-inclusion project signed by a lawyer, a first instalment that 'has to be paid today', a company that can no longer be used, a farm sold for R$ 4.8 million in the side agreement and R$ 3 million in the deed, a guide at Disney and two reservations in Paris. The money trail, according to the police.

pet-15504-04-quatro-mil-laudas.t: Four thousand pages in five days
pet-15504-04-quatro-mil-laudas.s: The police inquiry from May to September 2026: twelve annexes inherited from a search, an empty mansion with a bowling alley, two suspects who do not show up for the first summons, a police chief who explains why the concierge is a witness, a R$ 589 hard drive bought by the defence, two statements that leak and a prison without internet.

pet-15504-05-nao-confiavamos-em-ninguem.s: The director of supervision, the manager who wrote 31 letters to Master, the lawyer who signed the letter of invitation and the travel fixer. Four statements from people who watched from outside, with what each maintains, what each admits and what, 'looking back', each has come to think.

pet-15504-06-chegar-do-outro-lado.s: The three members of the WhatsApp group, each for hours, before the officer. The deputy who says he was told to 'hold off' and drafted 23 liquidation votes. The head who consulted the internal-affairs office without giving the amount or the name. The banker who answers 'directly, no' and calls the two of them angels. Three versions that fit the same messages.

pet-15562-01-cento-e-cinquenta-e-nove-pa.s: The request of 1 March 2026, signed by four police chiefs, that asked the Supreme Court for the third phase of Operation Compliance Zero. What the Federal Police say they found in the banker's phone: four fronts, an 'armed wing', an estimated R$ 52 billion loss to the deposit-guarantee fund and fourteen addresses, one of them belonging to someone who is not a suspect.

pet-15562-02-a-turma.s: A drone over the house in Nova Lima, a voice note asking for clearance at gate B and the visitor log that identified the retired Federal Police officer. Searches in the prosecutors' system with the user's name whited out, a screenshot of the police case system, an Interpol printout that Interpol does not recognise. And the bill: R$ 1 million a month for the 'Sicário', R$ 400,000 a month to be split six ways.

pet-15562-03-dar-um-sacode.s: The boat captain, the chef, the housekeeper who 'has to be ground down', the journalist who 'clocks in at 7' and the DJ in Miami: five conversations the police transcribed and say show how the banker dealt with people who displeased him, and what the police themselves admit they cannot say actually happened.

pet-15562-04-dezessete-de-novembro.s: A note on the phone with the names of the police chiefs at a closed meeting, another asking whether someone is close to the judge, an 'important' message from the lawyer at 7:28 am, a commissioned article at 7:41, a video call forced on the Central Bank at 1 pm and a jet at Guarulhos that night. How the police reconstruct the eve of the operation, and how the same meeting served to free the banker.

pet-15562-05-vinte-e-quatro-horas.s: Monday's order giving the Prosecutor General's Office one day, Tuesday's reply at 4:01 pm saying it could not be done, Tuesday night's ruling recording that the deadline had 'lapsed' at 3:18 pm, nineteen warrants, two targets who slept at another address and, on Friday, six pages from the Prosecutor General on what a deadline is, how many pages each petition had and a 'funeral event'.

pet-15562-06-as-caixas-lacradas.s: A service door broken down in Nova Lima, a Rolex, a R$ 190,000 necklace, three sheets with the acronyms of Federal Police directorates, two phones and two laptops handed over with their passwords. Then six months of petitions: the lawyer who cannot read the file, the supervisor who needs his laptop to answer the tax authority, the department head who gets a copy if he buys a sealed hard drive with the receipt.
